title: Research & statistics
summary: Everything below comes from replaying the bot's own code on 1-minute NQ data (2010-2026, New York time), 1 contract per piece, 0.75 pt cost per trade, using two periods: 2015-10 to 2023-10 and 2023-10 to 2026-10.

Every rule was found by looking at that same history, so the backtest overstates what to expect. Walk-forward and random-shuffle tests below estimate how much is real. Paper trade before risking money.

versions.name: Original (8 pieces)
versions.what: Opening Drive + upgrades, Monday long, Turn of Month, Small Dip (first 3 days), Month-end short, Thursday short, ORB retest 2R, First FVG

versions.name: v3 (+4 changes)
versions.what: Prior-day-low skip on the two shorts, First FVG direction filter, ORB 3R, calm-open long on any day (1% stop)
versions.qc: $586,038 net profit, 1,226 trades, worst day -$11,402 and max drawdown -$24,186 on 1 NQ

versions.name: v4 (+2)
versions.what: Big Dip Short and a 1.5% stop on the calm-open long

versions.name: v5 (current) (+1)
versions.qc: $821,474 net profit after $7,396 fees (821% return on $100k), about 1,720 round trips, PSR 99.939%, max drawdown -1,903 pts, worst day -792 pts, up to 5 contracts open

pieces.name: Opening Drive
pieces.rule: 09:00-10:00 move over 0.35 x range -> trade it at 10:00 (also when the 09:59 close is 0.2 x range past the overnight high/low). Stop at the first-hour extreme, capped at 0.6 x range; trail 0.4 x range after +0.5; one re-entry per day.
evidence: Walk-forward (settings chosen from earlier years only): 14,242 pts vs 15,135 with my settings (94%); the upgrades beat plain Opening Drive in 8 of 9 years
Extra cost it can absorb per trade before it stops paying: 22.9 pts
Tested and rejected: liquidity sweeps, Asia / London volume and range, EMA side, gap, drive size, first-hour volume, streaks, reversals, time exits, breakeven, later entries

pieces.name: Opening Drive re-entry
pieces.rule: Once per day: after Opening Drive is stopped / trailed out before 15:30, buy (sell) a break of the day's extreme since 09:00; stop past the low (high) since the exit.
evidence: Small: 81 trades over 11 years
Can absorb 10.6 pts extra cost per trade

pieces.name: Monday long
pieces.rule: Monday 09:30 if the last 5 sessions closed up. 1.5% stop, out 15:55.
evidence: Positive in both periods (+12.3 and +44.7 pts/trade)
Settings grid: the current 09:30 / 1.5% / 15:55 sits on a plateau, no better setting in both periods
Can absorb 21.4 pts extra cost per trade
Skipping on session-level context (sweeps, volume, EMA) was inconsistent between periods

pieces.name: Turn of Month
pieces.rule: First 3 sessions of the month if last month closed up (not on a Monday-long day). 1% stop, out 15:55.
evidence: Lost money 2015-23 (-3.8 pts/trade, -486 pts) and made +61 pts/trade since 2023
Loses in 2017, 2019 and 2022 - together with Thursday short it is the source of the 2019 losing year
Removing it from the whole bot costs +486 pts before 2023 but -3,362 pts after
No filter or setting I tried helped in both periods

pieces.name: Month-end short
pieces.rule: Last 2 sessions of a month that is up so far. Short 09:30, 1% stop, out 15:55. Skipped when the overnight range traded below the prior day's low.
evidence: With the prior-day-low skip rule: 2015-23 -155 -> +645 pts, 2023-26 +2,291 -> +2,179 pts, drawdown about halved
Same rule works on Thursday short, which makes it more believable
Only 31 trades in the recent period

pieces.name: Small Dip
pieces.rule: Calm open: dip from the 09:30 open (lowest low 09:30-09:44) at most 0.5 x its 30-day spread -> buy 09:50 on any day (was: first 3 sessions only). 1.5% stop, no target, out 15:55.
evidence: Random-days test: p = 0.063 (2015-23) and 0.0004 (2023-26); after correcting for the ~600 variants tried it is not significant (~0.17)
Walk-forward kept only 33% of the backtest points (3,895 vs 11,787) and lost in 2019, 2022 and 2024
Steadier-looking versions (first 15 min closed up, dip as % of range) were worse inside the whole bot
Can absorb 17.6 pts extra cost per trade
Second largest source of profit - the piece most likely to be partly overfitted

pieces.name: Big Dip Short
pieces.rule: If the 09:30-09:44 dip is more than 1.5 x its 30-day spread: short 09:50, 1% stop, out 15:55.
evidence: Random-days test: p = 0.008 and 0.006 (about 0.015 after correcting for ~30 variants)
Walk-forward kept 83% (6,735 of 8,115 pts); 7 of 9 years positive; the same settings were picked every year since 2022
Settings are on a plateau (stop, exit time, entry time, target all tested)
Buying the same dip lost money in both periods - the opening direction continues
Can absorb 9.6 pts extra cost per trade

pieces.name: Midday Follow
pieces.rule: 11:00-11:30: the first time the move since the 09:00 open is more than 0.5 x range, trade in that direction (next bar), 1% stop, out 15:55. One trade per day.
evidence: Random-direction test: p = 0.0004 and 0.0095 - the direction carries real information, it is not just market drift
Every trigger window I tried was positive in both periods (11:00-11:30, 11:00-12:00, 11:30-13:00, 12:00-13:00, 10:00-13:00)
Walk-forward kept 67% (7,929 of 11,851 pts); 7 of 9 years positive
A fixed 11:30 clock entry was fragile (12:00 collapsed) - this trigger version is not
Overlaps with Opening Drive on many days: skipping those days cost 3,400-6,900 pts for almost no drawdown relief
Can absorb 12.4 pts extra cost per trade

pieces.name: Thursday short
pieces.rule: Every Thursday 09:30, 1% stop, out 15:55 - skipped when the overnight range traded below the prior day's low.
evidence: Before the skip rule: -1,399 pts 2015-23; with it +1,535 pts, and 2023-26 +4,700 pts unchanged with 33% fewer trades and half the drawdown
Skip-rule p = 0.009 and 0.092 (about 0.12 after correcting for ~18 filters tried)
Of all weekdays, only Thursday is positive in both periods with the filter
Loses in 2019 (-534 pts)
Can absorb 17.5 pts extra cost per trade

pieces.name: ORB retest
pieces.rule: Uptrend days: first 10-minute close above the 09:30-10:00 range by 12:00, buy the 2-minute 20 EMA by 13:00. Stop 0.25 x range, target 3R (was 2R), out 15:55.
evidence: 3R target: +557 pts 2015-23 and +85 pts 2023-26 vs 2R - the only target change that beat 2R in both periods
Dropping the trend condition added trades but was inconsistent between periods
Can absorb 6.8 pts extra cost per trade

pieces.name: First FVG
pieces.rule: First 1-minute fair value gap 09:30-10:30 in the direction of the 09:00 move (>= 0.35 x range): limit at its middle, 2R target, out 15:55.
evidence: Almost no edge before 2023 (+0.1 pts/trade) and +5.4 since
Direction-filter p < 0.0001 in both periods; the filter lifted every neighbouring setting from about zero to positive
Far-edge entry looked great in my simulation but lost about 1,200 pts on 2023-26 in the bot's real code - rejected
Can absorb only 1.6 pts extra cost per trade - the most fragile piece (20% of all trades)
You currently have it switched off in settings

text: The whole history (9.3 years, 2,344 trading days) was reshuffled in 10-day blocks 2,000-4,000 times.
None of the 4,000 reshuffles lost money. With the same volatility but zero edge, chance made at most about 19,000 pts - the real result was 73,446.

Daily t-statistic 6.35, annualised Sharpe 2.08. Deflated Sharpe (discounting for how many variants were tried) still puts the chance the true Sharpe is above zero at 99.9% even if 10,000 variants had been tried (my variants were highly correlated, so this is generous).

Block-bootstrap range for 1 NQ: 56,000-92,000 pts total (5%-95%), about 6,000-9,900 pts a year; median worst drawdown -2,592 pts, worst 5% worse than -3,974 pts. That is deeper than the -1,903 pts that actually happened - plan around the deeper number.

Reading the chart: reshuffling spreads the profit evenly over the years, so the reshuffled lines rise steadily. In reality most of the profit came after 2020 (the strategy made little between 2015 and 2019), so the real curve sat below the typical reshuffle for most of the history and only caught up in 2025-2026. The reshuffle shows how much luck there is in the order of the days, not whether the edge will stay as strong as it has been recently.

walk_forward_text: For each year from 2018 to 2026, the settings were chosen using only the years before it and then traded in that year. 'Kept' is the walk-forward total as a share of the total with my chosen settings. Expect roughly 80% of Big Dip Short, 65% of Midday Follow and 35% of Small Dip, and about 94% of Opening Drive.
slippage_text: Net points over the full 2015-2026 history (6,171 trades) if each trade costs more than the 0.75 pts already charged. Real NQ / MNQ slippage is typically 0.5-1 pt per trade, so expect to keep about 90% from costs alone.

combine.text: Rough simulation of a Topstep $50K Combine (target $3,000, trailing max loss $2,000) from every possible start date, trading MNQ. It ignores Topstep's exact trailing-floor and consistency rules.

caveats: No untouched data is left: every rule was chosen while looking at both periods. The honest forward expectation is lower than the backtest - plan around about half until it has traded live.
Turn of Month and First FVG are the weakest pieces; Small Dip is the piece most likely to be partly overfitted.
Backtest fills assume a limit order fills when price touches it; real fills can be slower.
Up to 5 contracts can be open at once and the pieces often point the same way, so losses cluster.
On MNQ the full set has a drawdown of about $3,800 in the backtest - too large for a $50K Combine's $2,000 trailing limit; use fewer pieces (see the Combine table).
not_done: Not in the live bot: Gold, ES / YM. Retired (no edge): SD fade, AMD AM, AMD PM, Nowick wickless candles.

sensitivity.text: Each v5 setting was moved by about 20% on its own and the whole bot replayed. A real edge changes gradually; an overfitted one falls off a cliff. Largest drop: -11% on 2015-23 (Big Dip Short threshold 1.2). Most changes move the total by 0-5%, and no setting is more than 3.7% better than the one in use.

piece_head: Bad day for the piece (5% worst)
sizing.piece_text: Most pieces risk about the same per trade (a losing trade averages about 105-130 points, $210-260 on 1 MNQ). Only ORB retest (about $129) and First FVG (about $65) are smaller. Sizing each piece by its risk (ORB x2, First FVG x3 micros) lifted profit 15% but raised the drawdown 52% (-1,848 -> -2,800 points) and lowered profit per unit of drawdown from 28.3 to 25.3 recently and from 14.7 to 10.9 before 2023 - so equal sizing stays.
sizing.acct_text: Pass / bust rate from every possible start date, MNQ at $2 a point, with the trailing loss floor locking at the starting balance. Maximum drawdown at 1 MNQ each: all 10 pieces $3,697, 4-piece set $1,554, Opening Drive alone $1,355. Rule of thumb from the table: bust rates stay near zero while the maximum drawdown at your size is under about half of the account's max loss limit, and climb fast beyond about 60-70% of it. The 4-piece set is Opening Drive, Month-end short, First FVG and ORB retest.
